newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak FinMin offers 97 draft budget to parliament.
newsitem.headline: Slovak FinMin offers 97 draft budget to parliament.

text.p: Slovak Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik on Thursday presented to parliament his 1997 draft state budget, criticised by the opposition as anti-social, which foresees a 36.9-billion crown deficit.
"The budget is planned with revenues of 170 billion crowns and the expenditures at 206.9 billion, with an overall budget deficit of 36.9 billion crowns," Kozlik told parliament.
The proposed budget is based on 6.4-percent real gross domestic product (GDP) growth next year and 1997 inflation under six percent.
Next year's GDP should be about 660 billion crowns, he said.
The draft budget assumes some 25 billion crowns of the 1997 deficit for debt servicing.
Kozlik said that according to International Monetary Fund (IMF) standards, the 1997 fiscal deficit should total only about 11.658 billion crowns, representing 1.8 percent of the forecasted GDP.
The 1996 fiscal deficit, based on IMF standards, is expected to be total some 14.4 billion crowns, or 2.5 percent of GDP.
Slovakia's state budget deficit totalled 13.4 billion crowns for the January-September 1996 period, up from a 7.9-billion crown shortfall for the first eight months of this year.

Julius Brocka of the opposition Christian Democratic Union (KDH) said the budget's overall expenditures in the social sector were some 11-percent lower than in 1996, adding that this will hit the social situation of the population.
Brigita Schmoegnerova of the opposition Party of Demcoratic left (SDL) criticised lower subsidies in the budget for social insurance, which will have a negative impact on health care.

Schmoegnerova said the budget draft also reduces state subsidies to energy prices and transport services, which will result in higher prices in these sectors and create significant inflation pressures.
